DISTRIBUTED NETWORK PROTOCOL (DNP3) AUTHENTICATION AND AUTHORIZATION

THIS PROJECT WILL UPDATE COMMUNICATIONS STANDARDS, SPECIFICALLY THE DISTRIBUTED NETWORK PROTOCOL SECURE AUTHENTICATION VERSION 6 (DNP3-SAV6), THAT WILL PERFORM CENTRALIZED MANAGEMENT OF AUTHENTICATION AND AUTHORIZATION SERVICES IN A ZERO-TRUST ARCHITECTURE. THIS ADVANCE WILL BE SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE DNP3 IS PRESENTLY USED BY OVER 90% OF POWER UTILITIES IN NORTH AMERICA TO MONITOR AND CONTROL FIELD DEVICES, INCLUDING DISTRIBUTED ENERGY RESOURCES (DER), IN THEIR OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) NETWORKS.

SECURE TELECOMMUNICATIONS ARCHITECTURE FOR TRUSTED AND RESILIENT ELECTRIC COMMUNICATIONS STAR TREC

THIS PROJECT WILL RESEARCH, DEVELOP, TEST, AND DEMONSTRATE ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURES FOR A SECURE, STANDARDS-BASED, AND INTEROPERABLE PRIVATE 4G LTE AND 5G COMMUNICATIONS NETWORK DESIGNED TO MEET THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF ELECTRIC POWER SYSTEMS. THE DEVELOPED SECURITY ARCHITECTURE WILL BE APPLIED TO THE USE CASES OF INTEGRATING DISTRIBUTED ENERGY RESOURCES (DER) AND MICROGRIDS. ADDITIONAL SECURITY CAPABILITIES INCLUDE PROTECTIONS RELATED TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF DER COMMAND AND CONTROL.
MANAGEMENT AND OPERATIONS OF THE INL

UNIVERSAL UTILITY DATA EXCHANGE (UUDEX) INCREASES CAPABILITY WHILE REPLACING OUTMODED SERVICES AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE EXCHANGE OF DATA AND INFORMATION BETWEEN STAKEHOLDERS. THE UUDEX ARCHITECTURE IMPROVES TRUST THROUGH USE OF SECURITY ADVANCES, IMPROVES ROBUSTNESS AND RESILIENCY AND EASE OF EXTENSION USING MODEL-BASED DESIGN, AND IMPROVES PERFORMANCE AND SCALABILITY USING A PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE MESSAGING PATTERN.

THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE A DEMONSTRATION OF UUDEX’S CAPABILITIES AT AN INDEPENDENT SYSTEM OPERATOR (ISO) AND IN COMMUNICATION WITH ITS MEMBERS.
